subject: Economics
description: Income tax, corporate tax, capital gains, TDS, DTAA, new vs old regime

questions.stem: A direct tax is a tax that:

options.option_text: Is levied on goods and services consumed
Falls directly on the income or wealth of an individual / entity, with the burden NOT shifted to anyone else
Is paid only by salaried employees

questions.explanation: Direct tax — burden cannot be shifted; the legal taxpayer is the actual bearer. Examples: Income Tax, Corporate Tax, Capital Gains Tax, Securities Transaction Tax (STT), gift tax (now part of income tax). Indirect tax — burden shifted to consumer; examples: GST, customs duty, excise (now mostly subsumed in GST). India's tax buoyancy has improved post-2017 (GST rollout). Direct-tax-to-GDP ratio target: 6%+; FY 2023-24 actual ~6.6% — record level. Administered by CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) under Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The administration of direct taxes in India is the responsibility of:

options.option_text: CBIC (Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs)
SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)

questions.explanation: CBDT — statutory body under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963; under Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. Administers Income Tax Act 1961 + related laws. Headed by Chairperson + 6 members (IRS officers). CBIC — handles GST + Customs (since GST replaced the old Central Excise role). RBI — monetary policy + banking regulation. SEBI — securities market regulator. CBDT and CBIC together form the 'Two Boards' under the Department of Revenue.

questions.stem: Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares (held > 12 months) is taxed at the rate of (post-Budget 2024-25):

options.option_text: 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh exemption (revised in July 2024 budget)

questions.explanation: Budget 2024 (July 2024, post-elections) revised LTCG and STCG rates. LTCG on listed equity / equity MFs (>12 months): now 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh exemption (was 10% above ₹1 lakh). STCG on listed equity (≤12 months): now 20% (was 15%). LTCG on other assets (real estate, gold, debt MFs etc.): 12.5% (was 20% with indexation; indexation removed for transfers after 23-Jul-2024 except some real-estate grandfathering). Holding period harmonised: listed securities 12 months, all others 24 months.

questions.stem: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) on bank interest above the threshold is governed by which section?
questions.explanation: Section 194A — TDS on interest other than securities (bank deposits, etc.). Threshold raised in Budget 2025 — to ₹50,000/year (general; was ₹40,000) and ₹1,00,000/year for senior citizens (was ₹50,000). Common 194-series sections: 194 (dividends), 194A (interest), 194C (contractor), 194H (commission), 194J (professional fees), 194Q (purchase of goods >₹50 lakh), 194R (perquisites), 194S (virtual digital assets — crypto). Section 80C — deduction (not TDS); 234B — interest on default in advance tax; 10(14) — exemption on specified allowances.

questions.stem: The base corporate tax rate for domestic companies (NOT opting for 22% concessional regime, turnover > ₹400 cr) plus surcharge and cess is approximately:

options.option_text: 30% base, with 22% concessional rate available under Section 115BAA (no exemptions)

questions.explanation: Domestic companies (turnover > ₹400 cr previous year): 30% base + cess + surcharge ≈ 34.94% effective. Companies opting for 115BAA (introduced Sep 2019): 22% + 10% surcharge + 4% cess = 25.17% effective, but they must forgo most exemptions and deductions. New manufacturing companies (incorporated after 1-Oct-2019, started mfg by 31-Mar-2024) under 115BAB: 15%+10%+4% = 17.16%. Smaller domestic companies (turnover ≤ ₹400 cr in PY 2022-23): 25% base. Foreign companies: 35% base (post Budget 2024, reduced from 40%) + surcharge + cess.

questions.stem: DTAA (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement) is a bilateral treaty that:

options.option_text: Doubles the tax rate for dual-resident individuals
Prevents the same income from being taxed twice (in source country and residence country) and helps allocate taxing rights

questions.explanation: DTAA — bilateral; India has DTAAs with 90+ countries. Methods: (1) Exemption — income taxed only in one country; (2) Credit — both tax, but resident country gives credit for foreign tax paid. Mauritius DTAA was historically misused for round-tripping; renegotiated via Protocol 2016 (capital gains taxable in source country from 1-Apr-2017). India follows the OECD-modelled UN Model. GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rules) — overrides treaty if tax-avoidance is the main purpose. Section 90 of the Income Tax Act empowers the Government to enter into DTAAs.

questions.stem: The 'New Tax Regime' (Section 115BAC), made the default regime from FY 2023-24, is characterised by:

options.option_text: Higher slab rates and most deductions allowed
Lower slab rates BUT most deductions/exemptions (80C, HRA, LTA, etc.) NOT allowed; standard deduction allowed

questions.explanation: New Tax Regime — Section 115BAC, introduced Budget 2020, made default from FY 2023-24 (AY 2024-25). Lower slab rates but nearly all major deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, LTA, home-loan interest under 24(b), etc.) NOT allowed — only standard deduction (₹75,000 for FY 2024-25), employer NPS contribution (80CCD(2)), and family-pension deduction. FY 2025-26 slabs (post Feb 2025 budget): 0-₹4L nil; ₹4-8L 5%; ₹8-12L 10%; ₹12-16L 15%; ₹16-20L 20%; ₹20-24L 25%; >₹24L 30%. Rebate under 87A — full rebate up to ₹12L taxable income (so effectively no tax up to ₹12.75L with std deduction). Old regime still optionally available.
